transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I can’t seem to shut my brain off anymore. It starts with something small, like a client not responding to an email, and then within minutes I’m thinking I’m going to lose the contract, fall behind on my divorce payments, and never get back into a real leadership role. It just keeps going and I can’t get control of it.
Have you been avoiding any situations or activities because of these thoughts?

Yes. I’ve been avoiding or putting off things I used to just handle. Like networking follow-ups—I’ll think through every possible way it could go badly and then I just don’t send the message. Same with some client deliverables; I delay because I’m stuck anticipating problems.

And outside of work, I’ve pulled back from soccer and seeing friends. I’m embarrassed by how tense and irritable I’ve been, so I just don’t go.
Have you been feeling sad or hopeless about your future?
I don’t know that I’d call it hopeless. I get scared about the future a lot, and I can feel pretty down when I think about where things are headed, but it’s more worry than sadness, I think.
Have you been experiencing any physical symptoms like headaches or stomach issues when you're worried?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t clearly noticed headaches or stomach problems tied to the worrying. It’s more that I know I’m wound up, but I can’t point to a specific physical symptom like that.
Do you find yourself repeating certain actions or rituals to try and calm your worries?
Not really, no. I don’t think I have rituals or repeated actions like that. I mostly just get stuck thinking things over, but I’m not doing a specific routine to calm it down.
Has something very stressful or traumatic happened to you recently?
No, not that I can think of. Nothing recent that I’d call traumatic or some big stressful event. It’s more just… ongoing worry, I guess.
Is your worry spread across many areas of your life or is it mainly focused on one or two specific things?

It’s spread out across a lot of things. My mind jumps from contract work, to the mortgage, to worrying what people in the Bethesda tech circles think of me. Even something like a recruiter being slow to email back can feel like proof that my whole career is shutting down.
Do you think your worry is greater than what most people would experience in the same situations?

Yes, I think it is more than most people would have. I mean, my mind keeps jumping from contract work to the mortgage to whether people in the Bethesda tech circles think I’m damaged goods. Even if a recruiter is just slow to email back, I can take it as a sign that my whole career is closing down.
Do you feel like your worrying is interfering with your daily life or relationships?

Yes. It’s started getting in the way. I’ve missed networking follow-ups because I keep thinking through everything that could go wrong before I even send a message. And with client work, I’ve delayed deliverables for the same reason.

It’s affected people stuff too. I’ve pulled back from soccer and seeing friends because I feel embarrassed by how tense and irritable I’ve been.
How long have you been experiencing this kind of excessive worry?
It’s been about thirteen months now. It really started after I was fired, and honestly it never really let up, even once I found contract work.
Have you ever had a sudden feeling of intense fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes?
I’m not sure I’d describe it that way. I get very anxious, but I don’t think I’ve had it suddenly peak within a few minutes like an attack.
Do you experience any physical sensations, such as a racing heart or trembling, when you're in the midst of worrying?

Yeah. Mostly I feel really wound up and tense. My shoulders kind of lock up, and I feel like I’m bracing for bad news even when nothing is actually happening. I’ll pace around the house or bounce my leg during calls without really noticing it at first.
Do you find that specific, intrusive thoughts keep repeating in your mind as you worry?

Yes. It’s not like one single phrase over and over, but the same worries keep looping. I came in because I can’t shut my brain off anymore. It starts with something like a client not answering an email, and then pretty quickly I’m thinking I’m going to lose the contract, fall behind on divorce payments, and never get back into a real leadership role.
Was there something specific that happened around the time your excessive worry started, about thirteen months ago?
Yeah. It started after I was fired, about thirteen months ago. I thought it might settle down once I found contract work, but it really didn’t. It’s just kind of stayed there since then.
Is there usually something that triggers your worrying, or does it seem to come out of the blue?

It’s usually triggered by something, but the reaction feels way bigger than the thing itself. Like if a client doesn’t respond, I can’t just leave it there. Within a few minutes I’m thinking I’m going to lose the contract, fall behind on payments, and never get back into a real leadership role. It just keeps going, and I can’t shut it off.
When you're worrying, is it usually about something specific that could go wrong, or is it more of a general feeling of dread without a clear focus?

It’s usually about something specific that could go wrong. My mind jumps from contract work to mortgage payments to whether people in the Bethesda tech circles think I’m damaged goods. Even something like a recruiter taking too long to email back can start feeling like proof that my whole career is closing down.
Are there any specific situations or places that you avoid because they make you feel anxious or worried?

Yeah, I guess I’ve been avoiding some things. I’ve missed networking follow-ups because I start imagining every way the conversation could go badly. I’ve also delayed client deliverables when I get stuck worrying about what could be wrong with them.

And outside work, I’ve pulled back from soccer and seeing friends. I’m embarrassed by how tense and irritable I’ve been, so it feels easier to just not go.
Do you feel like your worrying is causing you a lot of distress?

Yes. It’s causing a lot of distress. It’s not just worrying in my head — it’s affecting what I actually do. I’ve missed networking follow-ups and put off client deliverables because I get stuck thinking through everything that could go wrong. And I’ve pulled back from soccer and friends because I’m embarrassed by how tense and irritable I’ve been.
Have you ever experienced a sudden, intense fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes, accompanied by symptoms like a racing heart or trembling?
I’m not sure I’d describe it that way. I do get really anxious, but I can’t think of a time where it suddenly peaked within a few minutes like that. It’s more like the worry builds and sticks around.
